title: Matplotlib Markers
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and main concepts of Matplotlib Markers.
Create a Matplotlib Figure and Axes suitable for the visualization task.
Apply the relevant plotting API and configure its key properties.
Inspect plotted artists or chart properties to verify the intended result.
Choose labels and visual encodings that communicate data accurately.
prerequisites: NumPy arrays and basic numeric data

understand.concept: Markers emphasize individual observations in a line plot. The marker argument selects a shape, markersize controls its size, and markeredgecolor and markerfacecolor style its outline and fill. Format strings can combine marker, line and color shorthand.
understand.whyItMatters: Markers make discrete measurements visible, especially when a line contains only a few observations.
understand.analogy: Markers are pins placed at each measured location along a route.
understand.summary: Matplotlib Markers is part of the Matplotlib learning path. The examples use deterministic data and the Agg backend for automated execution.

explain.narrative: Read the concept, execute each example in sequence, inspect the printed result and compare it with the expected output. Each example creates a figure with the non-interactive Agg backend and closes it after inspection.

examples.title: Choose circle markers
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 4], marker='o')
print(line.get_marker())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The marker property selects the point symbol.

examples.title: Set marker size
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 4], marker='s', markersize=8)
print(int(line.get_markersize()))
plt.close(fig)

examples.title: Set marker edge color
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 4], marker='o', markeredgecolor='red')
print(line.get_markeredgecolor())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The edge color styles the marker outline.

examples.title: Set marker face color
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 4], marker='o', markerfacecolor='gold')
print(line.get_markerfacecolor())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The face color fills the marker.

examples.title: Use a format string
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 4], 'g--o')
print(line.get_linestyle(), line.get_marker())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The compact format string combines green color, dashed line and circle markers.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small program demonstrating matplotlib markers. Use a deterministic dataset, configure the relevant chart properties, and print at least one check that verifies the result.
practise.independentTask: Apply the technique to a small dataset of your own. Include meaningful labels, check input lengths and explain why the chosen chart is appropriate.
hints: Start with a small deterministic dataset.
Create the Figure and Axes explicitly with plt.subplots().
Inspect the relevant artist or Axes property instead of relying on visual output alone.
Add labels and units that accurately describe the data.
Close figures after automated checks or file export.
practise.challenge: Build a reusable plotting function that validates its inputs, creates the requested chart, and returns or saves a well-labelled Figure without leaking open figures.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute under the pinned Python and Matplotlib environment and match expected output.
Examples use the intended Matplotlib API correctly.
The chart type and visual encodings match the data semantics.
Labels, legends and scales are accurate and readable where applicable.
Figures are closed after automated execution.

questions.prompt: Which argument selects the marker shape?
questions.explanation: marker selects symbols such as circles or squares.

questions.prompt: Which property changes the marker fill?
questions.explanation: markerfacecolor styles the inside of the marker.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of markeredgecolor?

questions.explanation: The final character specifies the marker symbol.
